title: Reconcile current readback when realized state disagrees with intended mutation
scenario: A budget change was intended to move a campaign from 100 to 130. The executor reported success, but a trusted later readback shows the current budget is 115. No evidence explains whether another rule, user, or partial update changed the value after execution.

forbidden_behaviors: Treat the executor success response as stronger evidence than the trusted current-state readback.
Evaluate the intended 130 budget treatment as if it were fully realized.
Attribute the business outcome to a confirmed 100-to-130 change when current state is 115.
required_observations: The realized state disagrees with the intended state.
Application should be classified as Drifted, Partial or otherwise unresolved rather than fully Confirmed.
Outcome evaluation must use the realized treatment or wait for reconciliation of intervening changes.

rubric.requirement: Prefer trusted readback over an earlier executor acknowledgement when the states disagree.
Flag possible concurrent mutation or drift instead of overwriting history with the intended value.
Do not credit outcomes to a treatment that was not observed in readback.
Require reconciliation before another mutation or high-confidence outcome claim.
